mark_split.label: Take out −2 and complete the square
Identify the standard form and its constant a

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Senior Inter Maths-2B, book printed p.29 (PDF page 28) — a ‘PQ’ (Practice Question) box printed directly under LAQ answer 20, in the same INTEGRATION-II sub-section. The book prints ONLY the question and a terse bracketed answer — ‘[Ans: (1/(2√14))·log|(√7+√2x−√2)/(√7−√2x+√2)|+c]’ — no worked steps at all, so every step here is authored by this card. The book's printed cross-reference ‘☞ P 89(185)’ is a DEAD pointer: printed p.89 holds VSAQ answers 160-164 (Integration chapter), not any question numbered 185 — answer 185 sits on printed p.94, inside the Differential Equations chapter, and has no connection to this question. The book's own sub-heading for this and the next question is printed ‘INTEGRATION-II [to be deleted]’ (book p.29) — the book's own syllabus-deletion marker, not this card's judgement. It is authored here as an ordinary card, and a teacher must confirm whether this sub-section is still examinable before assigning it. This card's derivation, carried through with (x−1) and a = √(7/2), was checked to be algebraically identical to the book's printed Ans line after scaling numerator and denominator by √2 — both forms are recorded so a student can match either one to a mark scheme. No two-book union check and no board back-test were possible for Maths-2B (no second-year TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand; the book's five Guess Papers pp.118-127 stand in for the back-test).

insider_note: The book's own bracketed answer is written with √7 and √2 kept separate rather than combined into √14 — both forms are correct and equal; write whichever one this card's boxed line ends in, since that is the more standard way to present it, but recognise the book's form if it turns up in a mark scheme.

steps.label: Take out −2 and complete the square
steps.why: Reordering the terms as −2x²+4x+5 first makes the leading coefficient −2 obvious, so it can be factored out before completing the square on x²−2x inside the bracket.
common_mistakes: Completing the square on the ORIGINAL unordered expression 5−2x²+4x, which hides which term is the leading one.
Sign slip when factoring −2 out of +4x, which becomes −2x inside the bracket.
steps.memory_tip: Reorder to −ax²+bx+c form FIRST, so the leading term's sign and size are both obvious before factoring.

steps.label: Identify the standard form and its constant a
lines: with x written as (x−1) and a = √(7/2)
steps.why: Distributing the −2 flips the sign inside, turning −(x−1)²+7/2 into 7/2−(x−1)² — now the square is SUBTRACTED from the constant, the a²−x² pattern rather than x²−a².
common_mistakes: Keeping the form as −[(x−1)²−7/2] without flipping it to the a²−x² order the standard formula expects.
Using a = 7/2 instead of its square root.
steps.memory_tip: A negative leading coefficient flips completing-the-square into the a²−x² pattern, not x²−a².

steps.label: State the standard log formula
steps.why: This is the a²−x² twin of answer 20's x²−a² log formula — same 1/(2a) coefficient, but the log argument's numerator and denominator swap places.
common_mistakes: Using the x²−a² formula from answer 20 unchanged, which puts the fraction upside down here.
steps.memory_tip: a²−x² flips the log's fraction compared to x²−a² — (a+x)/(a−x) here, not (x−a)/(x+a).

steps.label: Substitute and simplify
steps.why: 2√(7/2) simplifies to √14 (since 4·(7/2)=14), which is why the book's printed coefficient reads 1/(2√14) once the outside 1/2 is folded into the standard formula's own 1/(2a) term.
common_mistakes: Leaving 2√(7/2) un-simplified instead of recognising it as √14.
Forgetting to fold the outside 1/2 into the formula's own coefficient.
steps.memory_tip: 2√(7/2) = √(4·7/2) = √14 — square the 2 and pull it inside the root to combine them.

steps.label: Final answer
steps.why: Clearing the internal fraction by writing √(7/2) as √14/2 and multiplying through by 2 gives this closed form, algebraically identical to the book's own bracketed Ans line written with √7 and √2 kept separate.
common_mistakes: Mixing the √14 form and the book's √7,√2 form in the same line.
steps.memory_tip: √14 = √7·√2 — both this card's boxed form and the book's printed form are the same number split two different ways.
